model.title: A ray hits a mirror at 35° to the normal. Find the angle of reflection.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Angles are measured from the normal

questions.q: A ray hits a mirror at 20° to the surface. Find the angle of reflection.
questions.model: The 20° is from the mirror, not the normal. i = 90 - 20 = 70°. Law: r = i. So r = 70° from the normal.

questions.q: Why can't you see a reflection in a wall?
questions.a: Its rough surface gives diffuse reflection, scattering light.
A line at 90° to the surface where the ray hits.

questions.q: Core: Draw three ray diagrams with angles of incidence 30°, 45° and 60° and measure the reflected angles.
questions.model: Teacher draws the first: mirror line, dashed normal, incident ray at 30°, reflected ray at 30° on the other side.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why road signs use rough, matt paint but mirrors are polished.
questions.a: Matt paint gives diffuse reflection so signs are seen from many angles without glare; mirrors need specular reflection for a clear image.

questions.q: Stretch: Two mirrors at 90°. A ray hits the first at 30° to the normal. Find the angle it leaves the second mirror.
questions.a: It reflects at 30°, meets the second mirror at 60° to its normal, leaves at 60°, travelling back parallel to its original path.

questions.q: Angles in reflection are measured from the...
Big question: why can you see yourself in a mirror but not in a wall?
questions.a: The mirror is smooth (specular reflection, a clear image); the wall is rough (diffuse reflection scatters light).
